claims.text: High-temperature annealing induces atomic-scale short-range-order clusters in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The induced short-range-order clusters act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Pinning by short-range-order clusters produces a more uniform distribution of plastic deformation.
Short-range-order-mediated dislocation pinning increases the work-hardening rate.
Short-range-order-mediated dislocation pinning delays crack initiation.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits greater plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits greater toughness than commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy has a random atomic distribution with minimal pre-existing short-range order.
Annealing at approximately 1000°C can induce short-range order in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Varying the duration of a 1000°C anneal varies the amount of short-range order in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The density of atomic-scale short-range-order clusters can be quantified by atom probe tomography or high-resolution TEM.
Specimens with more pronounced short-range order will have greater plastic strain than both the as-cast HEA and pure tungsten.
Specimens with more pronounced short-range order will have higher work-hardening rates than the controls.
Specimens with more pronounced short-range order will initiate cracks later than the controls.
Specimens with more pronounced short-range order will absorb more energy before failure than both the as-cast HEA and pure tungsten.
The proposed short-range-order mechanism is applicable at approximately 1300°C in a controlled atmosphere when grain size and texture remain approximately constant.
